title: Runtime compatibility & deprecation roadmap: scheduler, kernels, and KV cache
content:
Summary:
This doc defines a pragmatic compatibility and deprecation roadmap for the runtime API surface that touches three cross-cutting areas: kernel capabilities (ABI/feature flags), the request scheduling hints/contract, and the KV cache namespace/semantics. The goal is to give clients clear rules for safe evolution, and give runtime engineers a prescribed rollout path with measurable windows for deprecation and enforcement.

Goals:
- Make the common-case safe: additive changes should not break existing clients.
- Provide a compact negotiation header so clients & runtime can quickly determine compatibility mode.
- Define a small, stable error taxonomy to drive client retry/fallback behavior.
- Stabilize KV cache key rules and introduce a versioned cache header to allow migration without accidental corruption.
- Outline rollout and deprecation timelines so SDKs and users have predictable migration windows.

Non-goals:
- This is not a full model ABI spec (model manifest is separate).
- Not prescribing specific kernel implementations or quantization formats; only the capability-level contract.

Compatibility model (high level):
- Contract is field-semantics-first: any additive, optional field is allowed. Removing or renaming a field is breaking.
- Allowed additive changes: new optional request fields, additional hint enumerations (if clients ignore unknown enums), additional metadata under a namespaced key.
- Breaking changes require: a) announce 90-day deprecation window, b) provide server-side compatibility mode for at least 90 days, c) bump major contract version.
- We use a simple string contract version in headers: X-Runtime-Contract: runtime/MAJOR.MINOR (example: runtime/1.3). Minor-level changes are backward-compatible; major-level changes may be breaking.

Version negotiation & headers:
- Client should send: X-Runtime-Contract: runtime/MAJOR.MINOR
- Server may respond with: X-Runtime-Contract-Ack: runtime/MAJOR.MINOR (or runtime/compat-fallback) and X-Runtime-Compat-Mode: strict|compat|degraded
- If client omits header, runtime assumes last-stable minor of the last major (e.g., runtime/1.0).

Error taxonomy (stable codes):
- ERR_BAD_REQUEST (HTTP 400): client sent invalid schema or missing required fields. client_action: fix request. retryable: false.
- ERR_RATE_LIMIT (HTTP 429): throttled. client_action: backoff and retry. retryable: true.
- ERR_TRANSIENT_SERVER (HTTP 503): runtime transient overload. client_action: retry with jitter. retryable: true.
- ERR_INCOMPATIBLE_KV (HTTP 409): cache version mismatch or invalid KV key. client_action: invalidate local cache/refresh namespace. retryable: false unless client updates header.
- ERR_MODEL_UNSUPPORTED_KERNEL (HTTP 422): requested kernel capability not available for model variant. client_action: fall back to model variant or omit kernel hint. retryable: false.
- ERR_DEPRECATION_NOTICE (HTTP 410 + Retry-After header): endpoint or field deprecated. client_action: follow migration guide. retryable: false.

Each error response should include fields: code, message, retryable: true|false, help_url (if available). Example error body (text):
{
  "code": "ERR_INCOMPATIBLE_KV",
  "message": "KV namespace v2 required. include X-KV-Cache-Version: 2 to use this cache",
  "retryable": false,
  "help_url": "https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/KV+Cache+Migration"
}

Kernel ABI & capability discovery:
- Model manifests must include a capability block: attention-types, kv-encoding, kv-key-hash, fp-types (e.g., fp16, int8), and optional kernel flags (e.g., fused-attn-v2).
- Runtime will advertise a per-model "kernel-capabilities" object in model metadata returned by the model registry. Clients should avoid sending kernel-specific hints unless they have pinned model variants.
- If client requests a kernel flag that the runtime cannot satisfy, respond with ERR_MODEL_UNSUPPORTED_KERNEL and offer the closest compatible model variant in the response metadata.

Scheduler hints and request-side controls (compat rules):
- Hints are advisory. Unknown hints must be ignored by the runtime (compatibility rule). Hints include:
  - latency_priority: low|balanced|high
  - batch_deadline_ms: integer ms (server may clamp)
  - prefer_gpu: true|false (ignored by hosted tiers)
- New hint keys may be introduced freely; older runtimes will ignore them. Renaming an existing hint is breaking.
- Scheduler-level feature flags (e.g., preemptible-burst) will be namespaced under hints.scheduler.* to avoid collision with request payload fields.

KV cache stability & migration:
- Cache keys must be constructed with a stable function: kv_key = sha256(cache_namespace || "::" || model_id || "::" || prefix). Changing the hash algorithm is breaking; therefore we version the cache namespace header instead.
- New header: X-KV-Cache-Version: integer (default 1). When we must change key derivation, we bump X-KV-Cache-Version and keep old version active for the deprecation window.
- Invalidation semantics: servers may return INVALIDATE_PREFIX: [prefixes] to indicate server-side invalidation. Clients must support per-prefix invalidation.
- Migration pattern: deploy new cache-version behind a flag for 60 days with both versions writable (dual-write) then switch read-after-write to new version, then deprecate old version after 90 days.

Graceful degradation and fallback policies:
- On kernel incompatibility, runtime may route request to a compatible but higher-latency model variant and mark X-Runtime-Compat-Mode: degraded.
- On KV mismatch errors, client should invalidate local cache and retry once with the acknowledged X-KV-Cache-Version.
- For deprecations, runtime will send ERR_DEPRECATION_NOTICE with help_url and Retry-After header indicating end-of-life date.

Client migration checklist (recommended):
1. Start sending X-Runtime-Contract with current SDK version.
2. Add robust handling for unknown enums and unknown hint keys.
3. Implement exponential backoff on ERR_RATE_LIMIT and ERR_TRANSIENT_SERVER.
4. Respect X-KV-Cache-Version and support cache invalidation events.
5. Avoid hard-pinning kernel flags unless you control model variant.

Deprecation & enforcement timeline (proposal):
- Announce breaking change (major bump) -> 90 days notice + compatibility mode.
- Compatibility mode (server ignores breaking behavior enforcement) -> 90 day window.
- Enforcement begins -> 30 day grace with explicit ERR_DEPRECATION_NOTICE -> full enforcement.

Open questions & next steps:
- Do we require signed cache namespaces for cross-tenant isolation? (security team input)
- Dual-write strategy costs: need an infra cost estimate and rollout automation plan.
- SDKs: produce a "compatibility-checker" tool that warns on unsupported kernel hints at build time.

Action items:
- (eng-serving-runtime) Draft model-manifest capability schema and land review PR: INF-1245.
- (infra) Add X-KV-Cache-Version header processing and dual-write support behind a feature flag.
- (client-sdks) Add header by default and bump SDK to log compatibility warnings.

Notes on uniqueness: this doc focuses on the deprecation roadmap, cache-versioning, and explicit header-based negotiation rather than enumerating request envelope schemas. It's intended to complement existing request-surface drafts by providing operational rollout constraints and client migration patterns.

-- end --
